safety_tips.tip: Stay Alert: Pay attention to what's happening around you, especially in crowded areas like markets, bus terminals, and tourist sites
Avoid Walking Alone at Night: Especially in less-trafficked or poorly lit areas. Take a registered taxi or ride-sharing service
Minimize Displays: Avoid flashing expensive jewelry, watches, cameras, or large amounts of cash
Beware of Pickpockets: In crowded areas, keep bags zipped and in front of you. Be especially careful in markets (like San Pedro Market)
ATMs: Use ATMs during daylight hours, preferably inside banks or well-lit, secure locations. Be mindful of anyone watching you
Bags: When sitting at a cafe or restaurant, don't hang your bag on the back of your chair; keep it on your lap or between your feet
Registered Taxis: Always use official, registered taxis (they usually have a taxi sign on top and company numbers on the side) or ride-sharing apps like Uber or Cabify when in Lima
Hydration: Drink plenty of water (bottled water only!)
Food & Water: Stick to bottled water. Be cautious with street food; choose establishments that look clean and have high turnover. Wash fruits and vegetables thoroughly
Good Samaritan Scams: Be wary of strangers who approach you offering unsolicited help, especially if they try to distract you

Fake Police: There have been reports of individuals posing as police officers to demand money or search tourists' bags. Always ask for official identification and never hand over your passport or wallet. If suspicious, insist on going to the nearest police station
Overcharging: Negotiate taxi fares before getting in, especially if not using a meter or ride-sharing app. Check restaurant bills carefully
